Every row below is therefore position management on the existing book — three closes (FCX, TLT, ITB), one take-profit in execution (XLE), one resting order cancelled before an earnings print (PYPL), one expired event contract retired, two stop widenings (IYR 100.40 to 100.50, DG 125.60 to 125.30) and five holds carrying new information (SMMT, HII, PFE, STLD, BCC). Position updates are not new risk and do not count against an idea target.

ONLY FIVE ROWS NEED AN ORDER TODAY, and they are not the top-ranked ones, because ranking is by conviction and reward-to-risk rather than by urgency: close FCX, TLT and ITB at the open, execute the XLE take-profit (sell half at the open, rest the balance at 70.50, be flat by Thursday's close), and cancel the PYPL 56.50 bid before Tuesday's pre-open print. The rest are holds.

TLT REVERSED MID-RUN, hold to close, and the reason is the most load-bearing thing in this report. The short's stated thesis was that the Fed is hiking, the 10-year is at 4.96% and December is live. All of it is true and all of it is priced — Kalshi has a December hike at ~80% — so the position had no edge over the market, and with 0.80 ATR of room before its stop it could not survive to collect the December SEP even if the view is right. The IYR short survives the same test only because its payoff rests on eleven constituents reporting this week rather than on the policy path, and that is stated in its own key_risk.

RATIOS CLUSTER JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR AND IT SHOULD BE SAID. Eight of the thirteen recomputed reward-to-risk ratios land between 2.00 and 2.23 against a 2.0 swing floor (TLT 2.00 exactly, FCX 2.02, PYPL 2.09, STLD 2.12, XLE 2.13, ITB 2.18, SMMT 2.19, DG 2.23). That is the signature this report is built to distrust. The mitigating fact is that these are previously published levels being managed rather than targets fitted this morning, and the three thinnest of them are being closed or cancelled today: TLT at exactly 2.00 and FCX at 2.02 are both exits, and ITB only ever cleared 2.18 on a stop 1.56 ATR from entry — widening it to the 1.8 ATR ETF floor drops the ratio to 1.89, so no publishable stop exists and the position is closed rather than re-cut. Expect the enforcement step to demote the ITB row to the watchlist for exactly that stop-distance failure; if it does, the instruction is unchanged and still live — COVER THE SHORT at Monday's open. A demoted row here is a position being exited, not an idea being withdrawn.

The two stop widenings move stops AWAY from entry and make the ratios worse (IYR 2.81 to 2.70, DG 2.30 to 2.23), which is the opposite of the pattern that made this check necessary. Both were corrections of stops sitting a hair inside the ATR floor: IYR at 1.75 ATR against 1.8, DG at 1.99 against 2.0.

COVERAGE GAPS. No VIX, no index level and no futures price of any kind — Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 for every index, futures, FX and commodity symbol, so SPX/NDX/DJI/RUT/VIX/ES/NQ/DXY/gold/WTI are all null and ETF proxies (SPY, QQQ, IWM, TLT, GLD) were used instead. No level was invented to fill the gap. Yahoo's options endpoint returned HTTP 401, so NO options-implied move was available for any name and the 'is this target inside what the market prices' check did not run once this morning. PFE's 2026-11-03 earnings date is carried forward from prior verification rather than re-confirmed, because it falls outside the four-day calendar window fetched. BCC's 65.00 bear case is derived from price structure (about 10% below the 72.06 60-day low) rather than from a defended valuation, which is below the standard this report sets for a long_term idea — it is flagged in that row's own key_risk and is why BCC is named the first position to cut. KLAC's valuation anchor was left incomplete rather than guessed, which is why it is a watchlist entry and not a recommendation.

EVENT CONTRACTS: none published, and for an honest reason rather than a blocker. The Kalshi list endpoint returns null prices, but the single-market endpoint does return live quotes — October is 93/6/1 and December is 75c for a hike, both deep and internally consistent against the KXFED target-rate ladder. Those prices look right, and taking the other side of December would require a core PCE forecast that was not made. Buying a 93c contract for a 7.5% two-day return is fair odds, not an edge. The one event contract on the book (KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5) resolved on 2026-10-14 and is retired here as expired-unfilled, not graded as a loss.

The Fed is HIKING — target range 3.75-4.00% after a September 2026 hike, effective funds 3.88% — with the 10-year at 4.96%, the 2-year at 4.65% and the curve re-steepened to +31bp. Kalshi prices Wednesday's hold at 93c on 3.23M contracts of open interest, and a December 25bp hike at 75c plus 5c for more, so roughly 80% of the hawkish path is already consensus rather than a disagreement anyone is being paid for. Everything whose cash flows are far away has been repriced: KLAC -32.2% off its 60-day high, INTC -31.8%, CCJ -29.5%, SMCI -28.0%, GEV -25.9%, BTC at $80,361. Everything that earns cash today sits at its highs: XOM -0.3% off its 60-day high, CVX -0.2%, KVUE -1.6%, MO -2.3%, GILD -2.8%, CL -3.6%. Last session fits — SPY -0.52% and IWM -0.33% with QQQ flat, mega-cap tech holding the index up while the capex chain underneath it falls. That read also explains this report's 3-of-27 closed record better than stock-picking does: every recent stop-out (CEG, GE, ITA, GDX, DAL) was long the de-rating side, and every position that is working (XLE, PFE, KHC, XLF) is on the cash-flow-today side. Both sides of the tape are badly priced for a new entry this week, which is why today's report is entirely position management.

recommendations.thesis: Take the profit on the 2026-08-15 long at 63.90, now +8.5%, and finish the job this week. This is a winner being closed near its target, not a thesis being abandoned. XLE closed at 69.33 against a 70.50 target - 1.7% away - and sits 0.56% under the 69.72 high of the fetched window, so substantially all of the move the idea asked for has been delivered. The reason to be flat by Thursday's close is sharper than it looked an hour ago: XOM is 24.04% of the fund and CVX is 18.32%, a combined 42.36% on State Street's own holdings as of 2026-10-23, and both report Friday before the open. XOM at 183.21 is 0.29% off its 60-day high and CVX at 233.21 is 0.23% off its own, both above their 20- and 50-day averages. So more than two fifths of the fund is priced for good news from two companies on one morning. Holding a nearly-complete 8.5% gain through that is paying full price for event risk after the thesis has already worked. Energy is also the single strongest thing on this tape - the one sector at its highs while the AI-capex chain is down 25-32% - and leadership is exactly when taking profit feels worst and reads best.
recommendations.key_risk: Selling the best-performing position in the book while it is still making highs is how a trend-follower gives up the fat tail: if XOM and CVX beat on Friday, XLE likely clears 70.50 and runs, and this exit will have capped the one idea that was working. The judgement is that 1.7% of remaining upside to target is not worth two mega-cap prints of gap risk on a position already up 8.5%, and the 42.36% concentration makes that gap risk a fund-level event rather than a diversified one. Note also that XLE has been published seven times in ten days - the most repeated symbol on the book - so the bias here runs toward holding it, and that is a reason to distrust any argument to keep it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that the regime favours it: with the Fed hiking and long duration being sold, energy is where cash flow today is being repriced upward, and XLE is in a confirmed uptrend above its 65.40 20-day and 64.34 50-day. Why sell leadership into a supportive macro? Because the horizon is wrong for that argument - this is a swing position with a 70.50 target now 1.7% away, not a long-term energy allocation. If the structural case is the real view, the honest expression is a fresh long_term idea with its own valuation anchor and accumulation zone, taken after Friday's prints at a price that reflects them, rather than a swing position quietly extended past its target because it is winning.

recommendations.thesis: Close the 2026-10-04 long at 68.20, now -4.4%. This is a thesis that stopped working being cut before a binary event, not a stop being honoured: every independent measure I can fetch has turned against it since entry. Analyst revisions are deteriorating — bullish share 80.0% to 76.7%, with a buy moved to hold in October. Insiders bought nothing in six months against five sales worth $8.39M net. And FCX has underperformed its own sector ETF XLB by 12.85% and SPY by 8.63% over one month, which makes this single-name operational weakness rather than a sector the market has turned on. Price at 65.18 is below both the 70.41 20-day and the 71.89 50-day and sits 18.8% off the 80.24 60-day high. The decisive point is structural: ATR14 is 2.5214, or 3.87% of price, and the 63.10 stop is only 0.82 ATR below spot. Holding into Tuesday is therefore not a bet on copper or on the quarter — it is a bet that the earnings gap is smaller than a normal day's range, which is a bet nobody should want.
recommendations.key_risk: FCX has beaten EPS four quarters running by 23-62%, so the probable headline is another beat and this exit can look foolish by Tuesday lunchtime. Accepting that is the point: what is being given up is a 0.82-ATR stop against an unquantified gap, and the right response to a position whose edge has gone is to stop paying for it rather than to hope the print rescues it. The secondary risk is that copper itself rips on a Grasberg supply shortfall — the same news that hurts Freeport's volumes can lift the metal — and this exit forgoes that, which is an argument for owning copper somewhere else, not for owning the miner with the broken mine.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that the de-rating IS the opportunity: 18.8% off the high on a copper franchise with a Grasberg mine-rights extension application filed, into a print the company has beaten four times running. The answer is that the market prices the ramp, not the quarter, and the ramp is contested in public. Freeport cut its near-term Grasberg recovery to about 65% of production in the second half from 85%, and targets full output by end-2027 — while the head of PT Freeport Indonesia said the full restart could slip to 2028, a characterisation Freeport publicly disputed on 2026-05-11 as misleading and reiterated 2027 in its quarterly filing. Ore at the block cave is wetter than expected and the chute needs modifying. When the company and its own Indonesian unit give different restart years in public, the ramp is not a variable I can handicap from outside, and Tuesday is when it gets updated.

recommendations.thesis: Hold the 2026-10-12 long at 262.00, now +4.6%, through Thursday's pre-open print. The long-term case is unchanged — HII is the sole builder of US nuclear submarines and aircraft carriers, and the holding is about converting a backlog measured in multiples of annual revenue rather than about any one quarter. What is new and genuinely supportive is the revision direction: analyst bullish share is 58.8% and improving by 5.9 points, the largest positive swing of any name on this book, in a sector that de-rated on budget and election risk rather than on programme news. The stock is still 18.07% off its 334.53 60-day high and sits below its 280.07 50-day while holding above the 267.09 20-day, so the de-rating has not reversed; it has stopped getting worse while the sell side turns. Relative strength fits the same picture: -23.72% over six months against SPY's +6.45%, but +3.04% over the past month against SPY's -0.94%. This is also one of the few positions in the book on the right side of the regime read — defense spending is cash-flow-today, not long-duration, and that is what is working in this tape.
recommendations.key_risk: A long-term position with no stop reporting in three days is the single most exposed thing on the book, and it should be named rather than smoothed over: Thursday's gap is unbounded in both directions and there is no order standing between the position and it. The specific vulnerability is that HII's problem has historically been execution, not demand — shipbuilding margin on fixed-price work, labour availability and schedule slippage are what have repriced this stock, and a quarter that misses on margin rather than on revenue is exactly the kind of news a backlog thesis cannot answer. Insiders give no comfort either: zero open-market buys against three sales. INVALIDATION, checkable rather than rhetorical: two consecutive quarters of shipbuilding segment margin contraction, or a material programme cancellation or deferral on the Virginia or Columbia class, or backlog declining year-on-year. Any of those closes the position regardless of price. A move to the 230.00 bear case on sentiment alone does not.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against holding through Thursday is simply that a stop-less position into a binary is indefensible on its own terms — it is the FCX objection, and FCX is being closed today for exactly that shape of risk. The distinction is real but it is narrower than it looks: FCX had a 0.82-ATR stop that would be resolved by the gap whether or not the thesis was wrong, whereas HII has no stop at all and therefore cannot be stopped out on noise; its risk is a permanent impairment of the backlog thesis, which a single quarter cannot deliver.
